result.title: Structural Agreement Indicates Prediction Accuracy For Protein-Ligand Co-Folding
result.comment: 30 pages, 9 figures, 20 supplementary figures, 3 supplementary tables. Code: https://github.com/oxpig/core-score
result.summary: Co-folding models predict the structures of proteins and their bound ligands, but their accuracy varies across targets. Their usefulness therefore depends on knowing which predictions a user can trust. Confidence scores are intended to guide that choice. However, across seven co-folding models, we show that confidence-based selection offers little improvement over choosing a prediction at random. For approximately three-quarters of structures, predictions are either exclusively correct or incorrect, leaving no opportunity for ranking to change the outcome. Moreover, high confidence does not reliably discriminate correct top-ranked predictions from incorrect ones. We find that structural agreement among predictions is a more accurate measure of likely success than current confidence scores. We capture this with the Concentration of Repeated Ensembles (CORE) Score, which combines cluster tightness with ensemble support. CORE Score discriminates top-1 success and oracle success, achieving mean ROC AUCs of 0.866 and 0.838, compared to 0.757 and 0.759 for ipTM. CORE Score also outperforms training set similarity measures, including ligand Tanimoto, protein sequence, and Runs N' Poses similarity, despite requiring no experimental ligand pose. Structural agreement is therefore a practical indicator of reliability and a baseline for evaluating future confidence estimators, without requiring an additional trained uncertainty estimator.

AI.brief_summary: 本文考察七种蛋白质-配体共折叠模型的置信度分数能否可靠筛选正确预测，发现基于置信度的选择几乎不优于随机，据此提出 CORE Score，用重复集成预测的结构一致性与聚类紧致度衡量可信度。
